elements.char: Abstract
elements.label: text

elements.char: —The discovery of the theory of compressed sensing
elements.label: text

elements.char: brought the realisation that many inverse problems can be solved
elements.label: text

elements.char: even when measurements are "incomplete". This is particularly
elements.label: text

elements.char: interesting in magnetic resonance imaging (MRI), where long
elements.label: text

elements.char: acquisition times can limit its use. In this work, we consider
elements.label: text

elements.char: the problem of learning a sparse sampling pattern that can be
elements.label: text

elements.char: used to optimally balance acquisition time versus quality of the
elements.label: text

elements.char: reconstructed image. We use a supervised learning approach,
elements.label: text

elements.char: making the assumption that our training data is representative
elements.label: text

elements.char: enough of new data acquisitions. We demonstrate that this is
elements.label: text

elements.char: indeed the case, even if the training data consists of just 7
elements.label: text

elements.char: training pairs of measurements and ground-truth images; with a
elements.label: text

elements.char: training set of brain images of size 192 by 192, for instance, one
elements.label: text

elements.char: of the learned patterns samples only 35% of k-space, however
elements.label: text

elements.char: results in reconstructions with mean SSIM 0.914 on a test set
elements.label: text

elements.char: of similar images. The proposed framework is general enough
elements.label: text

elements.char: to learn arbitrary sampling patterns, including common patterns
elements.label: text

elements.char: such as Cartesian, spiral and radial sampling.

elements.char: T
elements.label: text

elements.char: HE field of compressed sensing is founded on the re-
elements.label: text

elements.char: alisation that in inverse problems it is often possible
elements.label: text

elements.char: to recover signals from incomplete measurements. To do so,
elements.label: text

elements.char: the inherent structure of signals and images is exploited.
elements.label: text

elements.char: Finding a sparse representation for the unknown signal reduces
elements.label: text

elements.char: the number of unknowns and consequently the number of
elements.label: text

elements.char: measurements required for reconstruction. This is of great
elements.label: text

elements.char: interest in many applications, where external reasons (such as
elements.label: text

elements.char: cost or time constraints) typically imply that one should take
elements.label: text

elements.char: as few measurements as are required to obtain an adequate
elements.label: text

elements.char: reconstruction. A specific example of such an application is
elements.label: text

elements.char: magnetic resonance imaging (MRI). In MRI, measurements

elements.char: MRI, three underlying principles were identified that enable
elements.label: text

elements.char: the success of compressed sensing [2], [3]: 1) sparsity or
elements.label: text

elements.char: compressibility of the signal to be recovered (in some sparsi-
elements.label: text

elements.char: fying transform, such as a wavelet transform), 2) incoherent
elements.label: text

elements.char: measurements (with respect to the aforementioned sparsifying
elements.label: text

elements.char: transform) and 3) a nonlinear reconstruction algorithm that
elements.label: text

elements.char: takes advantage of the sparsity structure in the true signal.

elements.char: curately reflect the true structure of the signal: the typical
elements.label: text

elements.char: convex reconstruction problem can be replaced by a dictionary
elements.label: text

elements.label: text

elements.char: information obtained from one contrast can be used to inform
elements.label: text

elements.char: a regularisation functional to use in the other contrasts [5]; and
elements.label: text

elements.char: in dynamic MRI additional low rank structure can be exploited
elements.label: text

elements.char: to improve reconstruction quality [6], [7].
